source: Authored synthetic connected episodes, not observed customers

cases.story: One auditor has separate Payments/Billing grants. Payments changes managers without moving Billing authority or revoking an already approved customer grant.
A settlement patch genuinely fails independent tests. Its author transfers to CRM; a remaining teammate fixes it and a new authorized colleague reviews the exact replacement.

A first administrator leaves CRM before quorum completes. Only the two currently eligible exact reviews activate access; an excluded review cannot replace a selected signer whose sessions are revoked.
A queued Billing check loses its engineer before dispatch. It saves superseded evidence without executing; a peer explicitly retries and obtains fresh actual checks.
Billing temporarily loses its manager. The backup lead retains only Billing; restoring the original account does not revive old sessions.
A Deals access proposal expires while a review is delayed. Neither late approval nor refresh extends the original expiry or creates a grant.
Payments expires on the actual clock while Billing remains accessible. A new explicitly approved Payments request restores access; old approval replay never revives the expired grant.
A completed-state restart preserves failed checks, selected reviewers, expired grants and exact reviewed handoffs. Refresh dispatches no model or replacement check.
